chapter.chapter: Chapter 4 — Principles of Inheritance and Variation

excerpts:
[NSEB 2015 — question paper]
52. Study the following pedigree. The transmission of the trait indicates:
a) X-linked inheritance.
b) Autosomal dominance.
c) Autosomal recessive type.
d) Mitochondrial inheritance.

[CBSE Class XII Biology, sample question paper, 2022-23]
14. Assertion: When white eyed, yellow bodied Drosophila females were hybridized with 1
red eyed, brown-bodied males; and F1 progeny was intercrossed, F2 ratio deviated
from 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
Reason: When two genes in a dihybrid are on the same chromosome, the
proportion of parental gene combinations is much higher than the non-parental type.

[CBSE Class XII Biology, marking scheme, 2025-26]
6. C. Hardy-Weinberg principle says that phenotype frequencies in a population 1
are stable and are constant from generation to generation.

[CBSE Class XII Biology, sample question paper, 2022-23]
29. and 30 are case based questions. Each question has subparts with internal choice in one
subpart.
29 Study the Pedigree chart given below and answer the questions that follow: 4
(a) On the basis of the inheritance pattern exhibited in this pedigree chart, what
conclusion can you draw about the pattern of inheritance?
(b) If the female is homozygous for the affected trait in this pedigree chart, then
what percentage of her sons will be affected ?
(c) Give the genotype of offsprings 1,2,3 and 4 in III generation.
OR
(c) In this type of inheritance pattern, out of male and female children which one
has less probability of receiving the trait from the parents. Give a reason.

items.stem: What is the main reason Mendel's work was significant in the field of genetics?
Based on the passage, what does the term 'variation' refer to in the context of genetics?
In a cross between a true-breeding red-flowered plant and a true-breeding white-flowered plant, all the offspring have red flowers. What can be concluded about the red-flower trait?
If a plant has the genotype Tt, what will be its phenotype according to the passage?
Based on the diagram in Figure 4.3, which of the following represents the genotype of the F1 generation in a monohybrid cross between TT and tt plants?
If a plant is heterozygous for a trait (Tt), why does it express the dominant trait (T) and not the recessive one (t)?
In a monohybrid cross, a plant with genotype Tt is crossed with a plant with genotype tt. What will be the genotypic ratio of the offspring?
A test cross is performed between a tall plant (unknown genotype) and a dwarf plant (tt). If all the offspring are tall, what can be concluded about the genotype of the tall plant?
In a monohybrid cross between a tall plant (Tt) and a dwarf plant (tt), what is the expected phenotypic ratio of the offspring?
In a monohybrid cross, a plant with genotype Tt is crossed with a plant with genotype Tt. What will be the genotypic ratio of the offspring?
Which of the following is an example of co-dominance?
In a dihybrid cross between a plant with yellow round seeds (YYRR) and a plant with green wrinkled seeds (yyrr), which of the following would be the genotype of the F1 generation?
In a monohybrid cross between a heterozygous tall plant (Tt) and a homozygous dwarf plant (tt), what is the expected phenotypic ratio of the offspring?
What is the phenotypic ratio observed in a dihybrid cross according to the passage?
If a dihybrid cross shows a deviation from the 9:3:3:1 ratio, what is the most likely explanation according to the passage?
In a dihybrid cross, if the F2 generation shows a 9:3:3:1 ratio, what does this indicate about the genes involved?
What did Morgan observe about the proportion of parental gene combinations when genes were on the same chromosome?
Based on the information in the passage, what can be inferred about the inheritance pattern of a trait that is more common in males than females?
If a dihybrid cross shows a deviation from the typical 9:3:3:1 ratio, what could be the reason?
What is the term used to describe the change in a single base pair of DNA?
If a person has an autosomal recessive disorder like phenylketonuria, what must be true about their parents?
If a gene is located on the X chromosome and is recessive, which of the following is most likely to express the trait?
A couple has a child with Down syndrome. What is the most likely cause of this condition?
In a family, a mother is a carrier for a recessive genetic disorder and the father is unaffected. What is the probability that their child will be affected by the disorder?
Which of the following is a characteristic of an individual with Klinefelter’s syndrome?
In a family with a history of thalassemia, a child is born with the condition. If the parents are both carriers, what is the probability that their next child will be unaffected?
Which of the following is a Mendelian disorder?
In a family, a woman is a carrier for haemophilia and a man is affected. What is the probability of their daughter being a carrier?
In a pedigree analysis, what does a filled-up square represent?
In a dihybrid cross, if two genes show a higher proportion of parental gene combinations, what can be inferred about their linkage?
In which type of sex determination do males produce two different types of gametes?
What is the term used for the units of inheritance that carry information for a particular trait?
Which of the following is an example of a trait that Mendel studied in pea plants?
Which of the following is a true-breeding line?
What is the term used to describe the physical expression of a trait in an organism?
What is the term used for genes that are located on the same chromosome and tend to be inherited together?
If a true-breeding tall pea plant is crossed with a true-breeding dwarf pea plant, what is the likely outcome in the first generation?
If a carrier female for colour blindness marries a normal male, what is the probability of their son being colour blind?
